clean_text: Lines are off and the Ginny is still afloat. Forty fares are calling that a success.
name: Casting off — Cra-Zi Landing
open: Lines off. Forty fares booked for Nowhere. Three days. It is always three days.

unresolved_text: The channel closes to a hippo's width. One of them leans on the hull, politely, and the old girl feels it for a mile.
clean_text: The pod lets you pass. One of them yawns, and you decide to take it as permission.
name: The Hippo Shallows
open: Brown backs surfacing in the shallows, and the channel narrowing to something a piano could touch both sides of.

unresolved_text: The cut takes a stripe of paint off one side and a little more off the other. The rock does not apologise.
clean_text: Out the far end of the cut with both walls where you left them. The paint, less so.
name: The Narrow Cut
open: Two walls of black rock and a bend you cannot see past. No reverse. We're going in.

unresolved_text: The Ginny touches the bar. A long groan runs through her, and the Calliope, to her credit, does not say 'told you so.'
clean_text: You slide past the Calliope without touching the bar. She watches you go, the way she watches everyone.
name: The Calliope

settle_stages.text: A steam launch on her side in the mud, listing hard, boiler still faintly hissing. Nobody has ever come back for her.
The Calliope is down to her rail now. Stack still standing. Still, faintly, venting.
A stub of stack and some birds. You have to know where to look, and you do.

unresolved_text: The wall turns her for you. There is a sound like a cathedral door, and every passenger decides to remember it.
clean_text: You bring her round in the dark and out the way you came. The wall never got a word in.
name: Ilostmi Mine
open: Dead end. The adit is a cul-de-sac and the Ginny will not back out. The only way home is the way you came — you turn her with the helm while you still have way on, or the wall turns her for you. There is ore if you get out clean.
brief: She will not reverse. Almost every beat belongs on the helm. A joke is a luxury. The buckets will not turn the boat.

station_copy.steer: Helm over. No reverse — you are turning her with what way she has left. The wall is still there.
station_copy.wrench: You go below. The wall does not care that you are oiling something.
station_copy.bail: You hand out buckets in a hole with one exit. The water goes down. The boat does not turn.

unresolved_text: The shoal was not on the chart, and the keel tells you so in a low voice.
clean_text: The Reach is as wide as the chart claimed, which unsettles you more than a shoal would.
name: The Reach
open: Open water. The chart is generous about this stretch, in wording it clearly did not read back.

unresolved_text: A snag finds the hull and rakes along the planking with the sound of a very long fingernail.
clean_text: You duck, the timber misses, and every passenger looks at the wrong thing. Perfect.
name: The Snag Field
sub: The chart does not mention a fence
open: Timber in the channel, laid down like a fence somebody forgot to take in. You will duck. They will look at the wrong thing.

unresolved_text: The bend is empty and everyone knows it. The room wanted teeth and got a lecture on tides.
clean_text: No crocodiles. The passengers have opinions. You let them have the whole bend.
name: Crocodile Bend
open: The chart marks this stretch CROCODILE. The water is empty. The passengers came for teeth. They have opinions about the lack of teeth.

unresolved_text: The race takes the Ginny sideways, spins her once, and sets her down without comment. Something in her aches.
clean_text: The race tugs, thinks about it, and lets go. The mill, wherever it is, is not impressed.
name: The Old Race
sub: The mill is gone. The water is not.
open: A mill race with the mill long gone. The water still thinks it has a job, and it is doing that job at you.

unresolved_text: The landing is slick. A passenger sits down hard on a step that is not on the chart. The shrine has seen worse.
clean_text: They photograph the shrine, misspell it, and photograph the misspelling.
name: The Unnamed Shrine
sub: A landing. A name that isn't on the chart.
open: A stone landing and a shrine to a name that isn't written down. They want a photograph of something they cannot spell.

name: Knight Falls
open: There it is. Nine feet of water falling 108 inches. Forty passengers who paid for a legend.

station_copy.bail: This expedition is going underwater, fast.
station_copy.steer: The falls are not a channel. You keep her pointed downstream. The gauge eases. You are not parked.
station_copy.wrench: You go below during the advertised bit. They came for a waterfall.

unresolved_text: You clip a skiff. Eleven clay boats go into the river, and a good deal of the Ginny's paint goes with them.
clean_text: You thread the skiffs without buying a single clay boat. It takes more discipline than it sounds.
name: The Floating Market
sub: Forty skiffs. Every one a souvenir stall.
open: A floating market: forty skiffs, and every one of them selling something you cannot use. They wave. They are very close. They have heard about you.

unresolved_text: Something solid appears in the fog about a second after you hit it. You are not sure what. The Ginny is.
clean_text: The fog thins and there is the river, right where you guessed it. You will not mention the guess.
name: The Fog Bank
open: Fog, thick as wet wool, and the chart insists the river is clear. You can hear things. For the most part, they are the river.

unresolved_text: The bridge takes the top off something. The awning, a hat, the Ginny's good name.
clean_text: Under the arch with a finger's width to spare. Somebody's hat was less fortunate.
name: The Low Bridge
sub: Three arches. The chart says four.
open: A stone bridge, a hundred years old and a good deal lower than advertised. The middle arch is a rumour. Mind your heads.

unresolved_text: The chop gets under her. Every rivet makes a small complaint, and a few make it permanent.
clean_text: The chop gives out and the Ginny rattles on. Everything aboard is in a slightly different order.
name: The Washboard
sub: Water that has lost its temper
open: Water that has lost its temper. Everything on the boat begins to rattle in a different key.

unresolved_text: The shallows take the keel for a moment. The man on the island stops waving, which is somehow worse.
clean_text: The man on the island waves. You wave. Nobody has ever been so well received for so little.
name: The Waving Island
sub: One tree. One man. He waves.
open: A tiny island with one tree and one man, who waves like it is his job. It is. He has been paid to wave since 1898.

unresolved_text: The cable catches the funnel and sings. The ferryman looks up for the first time in years.
clean_text: You slip under the cable with a hand's breadth of daylight. The ferryman does not look up.
name: The Cable Ferry
sub: The cable is at neck height
open: A cable ferry, the cable pulled taut across your channel, and a ferryman who is very sure it is your move.

clean_text: The orange settles and the river is brown again. Several passengers say nothing, which is how you know.
name: The Butterfly Bank
open: A cloud of butterflies lifts off the bank as you pass, so many that for a moment the river is orange and the skipper is a little emotional.

unresolved_text: You pass too close and the Kettle Rocks boil over onto the deck. Nobody is hurt. Everyone smells of eggs.
clean_text: The Kettle Rocks mutter and let you go. Not a drop of tea.
name: The Kettle Rocks
sub: They boil, if you are patient
open: Two rocks stacked like a kettle and its lid. It has been on the boil, locals say, since before the river had a name.

clean_text: The jury watches you pass and files no comment.
name: The Pelican Parade
sub: Eleven pelicans. All of them in charge.
open: Eleven pelicans on a sandbar, standing in a line like a very patient jury.

unresolved_text: A bedsheet takes you full in the face. Then a second. A passenger emerges wearing someone else's trousers.
clean_text: You duck the line and a sheet brushes your hat. A village has a clean week and does not know how close it was.
name: The Washing Line
sub: Someone's whole week, over the water
open: A village has strung its washing clean across the channel. Shirts. Sheets. A flag that is plainly somebody's trousers.

clean_text: The statue bows. So do you. It seems only fair.
name: The Bowing Statue
open: A stone figure the height of a church, bowing deeply to the water, as if it has just been told something.

clean_text: The paper moons fall behind you. The village goes on waving at the dark.
name: The Lantern Village
open: Strings of paper lanterns across the water, and a village that stays awake for the boats. They are very well rehearsed.

clean_text: The otters go down the slide one more time, for no one.
name: The Otter Slide
open: A mud slide, and otters using it with total commitment. They do not look at the boat. They know you are watching.

unresolved_text: A heron takes a hat. Then a sandwich. By the time you look up, they have taken the principle of the thing.
clean_text: Every hat is still on every head. The herons make a note.
name: The Heron Rookery
sub: They have your hats in mind
open: Tall grey herons in the dead trees, every one watching your passengers' hats and sandwiches.

unresolved_text: The bell buoy bongs off the hull. Everyone says 'ah.' The shoal, smug, has been there the whole time.
clean_text: The bell tolls once more and you are past the shoal. It was not on the chart, and it was right.
name: The Bell Buoy
open: A bell buoy tolling in the middle of nowhere in particular, marking a hazard the chart does not.

unresolved_text: Loose rock comes down on the boat from the Thursday blast. The Ginny wears a few of the stones for a mile.
clean_text: The blast comes a hundred yards behind you. Thursday would like to apologise.
name: The Old Quarry
open: A quarry on the bank, and a bell that rings before they blast. It is ringing. It is Thursday.

unresolved_text: The steam rolls over the boat. Everyone is very warm, and the boiler is smug about it.
clean_text: The steam rolls by. The boiler glares at it and says nothing.
name: The Hot Spring
sub: Steam, and a boiler with ideas
open: A hot spring steaming on the bank. The boiler appears to have noticed.

unresolved_text: The squall catches you broadside. Rain comes in from every direction at once, and a surprising amount of it ends up inside.
clean_text: The squall moves on down the valley, looking for somebody else. Everything aboard is wet in a new way.
name: The Rain Squall
sub: It came from nowhere. It is going there too.
open: The sky goes dark in a single breath, and the squall comes down the valley like it has been waiting for you.

clean_text: The light goes. The phones are put away. For a moment nobody is documenting anything.
name: The Golden Hour
open: The light goes gold and the river becomes a postcard. Forty cameras appear. They are all pointed at the wrong thing.

unresolved_text: A hulk reaches out and takes a piece of you as a keepsake. It is mutual; it was already missing a piece.
clean_text: You sail through the hulks with a lighter touch than the rest of them had.
name: The Boat Graveyard
open: A bank full of hulks, every one a boat that thought it knew the way.

clean_text: He raises one hand. You raise one hand. That is the whole conversation, and it is plenty.
name: The Hermit's Dock
open: A man on a tiny dock, who raises one hand to the boat in what could be a greeting or a long-held objection.

clean_text: The cliffs finish their chord and the wind goes back to being wind.
name: The Singing Cliffs
open: Pale cliffs full of holes, and the wind whistling through them in chords nobody asked for.

unresolved_text: The dredge's arm catches the rail, groans, and lets go. Fifty years of rust, and it still has a grip.
clean_text: The great arm stays up. Whatever it was asking, nobody has answered.
name: The Sleeping Dredge
open: A rusted dredge, half sunk, its great arm lifted over the channel like a hand waiting to be asked a question.

unresolved_text: The nets wrap the rudder. The fishermen free you with the patience of men who are, and always have been, right. The room does not enjoy it.
clean_text: You pass between the nets without disturbing a single fish. They would like it known they noticed.
name: The Fish Weirs
sub: Nets, and the people who mind them
open: Fishing weirs strung across the channel in neat lines. The fishermen watch you with the calm of men who are in the right.

clean_text: The cabbages rock gently in your wake. No scarecrow files a complaint.
name: The Floating Gardens
open: Rafts of vegetables drifting in rows, each with a tiny scarecrow in charge.

unresolved_text: The inspector holds you up for forms. The forms have forms. The room watches the sun move.
clean_text: The stamp comes down, the inspector nods, and you are through. Nobody asked for your papers.
name: The Customs Post
open: A little customs post on a jetty, and an official with a stamp who has been waiting for you personally.

clean_text: You pass the surveyor's hut. The pencil is still on the table, and so is the afternoon he got it all wrong.
name: The Surveyor's Hut
open: A small hut on the bank with a drawing table in the window. Nobody has moved the pencil. You can see the afternoon he got everything wrong.

unresolved_text: The dragonflies find the passengers. There is a good deal of swatting, and some of it connects.
clean_text: The dragonflies lose interest all at once and move on. You swallow only one.
name: The Dragonfly Swarm
open: Dragonflies, thousands of them, and every one has decided the boat is the most interesting thing in the valley.

clean_text: You glide past the smokehouse. Lunch will have to remain an abstract idea.
name: The Smokehouse
open: A smokehouse on the bank, a column of smoke going straight up, and a smell that softens a skipper's resolve.

unresolved_text: You kiss the steeple. A cloud of old plaster, one startled gull, and from a fathom down, a single 'bong.'
clean_text: You steer round the steeple. The bell, a fathom down, says nothing, which is the right thing.
name: The Drowned Steeple
open: A church steeple standing out of the water, the bell still in it. You steer round, and for the length of a breath nobody says anything.

unresolved_text: A child lets go at exactly the wrong moment. The splash arrives from above, the boat is entirely under it, and forty people are wet in a new way.
clean_text: The children miss you by a boat's width and shriek their disappointment.
name: The Rope Swing
open: Children on a rope swing, launching themselves off the bank, and a boat that is, from their point of view, a target.

unresolved_text: The wall of water takes the Ginny broadside and sets her down hard. Water everywhere, including places that were dry on purpose.
clean_text: The wall of water lifts the Ginny, sets her down, and goes on up the river, unbothered.
name: The Tidal Bore
open: A wall of brown water comes up the river toward you, in no hurry, absolutely certain.

unresolved_text: The barge's wake takes the Ginny's shoulder, and then the barge itself, gently, takes the rest. The captain does not look down.
clean_text: The barge goes by like a village changing its mind. The captain gives you the nicest look he has.
name: The Slow Barge
open: A coal barge the size of a village, doing two knots in the middle of the channel, and its captain has seen your boat before.
